plan: dispatch://INFRA-743/artifact/plan-md (version 1). It is the whole plan: what main does today with citations, the design (D1-D6), the ordered tasks with their files, the tests, the acceptance-to-surface-to-command table, the sibling pull requests, the risks and the skills.
summary: The retry Acceptance 2 asks for already exists on main (bus.recoverUntilHealthy retries the reconnect hooks with backoff until they succeed or the client stops). What is missing is the report: a self-repaired rewatch failure is logged at ERROR (internal/bus/recovery.go:86, and internal/kvwatch's reportFailedRepair), and a rewatch that keeps failing while the watcher has not yet ended is invisible to /healthz. The plan records how long the hooks have been uncovered on bus.Client, states one bound (bus.RepairGrace, a minute, shared with kvwatch's unrepairedDelay), reports a failure under the bound at WARN and past it at ERROR, and answers 503 on /healthz naming 'KV watch rebuild' once the stall passes the bound.

skill://legion-worker/references/cleanup-deletion.md: the change deletes reportFailedRepair and repairFailedReason from internal/kvwatch and their call sites, so the deletion must carry every caller, comment and test with it.
skill://asd-ste100: the Envoy message to the INFRA-514, INFRA-590 and INFRA-594 roles is a message another agent reads.

skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md#what-a-proof-is: each proof entry needs criterion, surface, command, observed, headSha and negativeControl, which the 200-run loop and the /healthz smoke must each carry.
docs/testing.md: this repository's test rules that the code does not show (unix socket paths in Go tests), which the new cmd/listener and internal/bus tests must follow.

findings.finding: The spec's Evidence ('the reconnect hook gives up on one deadline-bound watch attempt, so a listener can keep serving a cache that no longer follows the bucket until the next reconnect') is contradicted by main: recovery.go:88-93 starts a recovery for the same connection event and recoverUntilHealthy (recovery.go:250-317) retries the hooks with backoff until they succeed or the client stops.
findings.answer: Recorded as the plan's one spec departure (section 1) and reported to the architect; the plan builds no second retry. The work goes to what is missing: the severity of a self-repaired failure and the bound plus health signal for one that is not self-repairing. The planner ran recovery_test.go:373 at the base to confirm: PASS.

findings.finding: Acceptance 1's other two clauses (a live watch, current caches) already hold on main, so the deterministic test can fail on main only on its ERROR assertion; a test failing on data would have to race a real JetStream deadline.
findings.answer: Stated plainly in the plan (decision 3 of section 2) and required in the test's own comment and in the PR body, so no reader takes the test for a behavioural regression test.

findings.finding: internal/kvwatch already answers the same question differently: Rewatch calls reportFailedRepair on every failure path, which logs ERROR '<name> watcher was not repaired' at once when the watcher had stopped (kvwatch.go:199-215, 651-689), under the decision INFRA-182 recorded. A bus-only change leaves that ERROR for a retry that later succeeds.
findings.answer: In scope: D4 deletes reportFailedRepair and repairFailedReason, leaving the wait armed at the stop as the one report, and rewrites the comment at kvwatch.go:594-603. The plan cites INFRA-182's block b-9cd21ccd and says which half of that decision is refined and why (another repair is armed within seconds).

findings.finding: A new 503 on /healthz has a blast radius (GKE readiness takes the pod out of the Service about 10 s after the grace; the ECS container health check replaces the task after about 90-120 s) and is moot in most JetStream outages, where the 3 s ping check already answers 503.
findings.answer: Decision 1 of the plan: 503, with the alternative (degraded 200) named and rejected because no probe reads it. The narrow band it adds is exactly this issue's band: STREAM.INFO answers while consumer creation does not. Liveness and startup read /livez, never /healthz, so no pod is restarted; delivery semantics are untouched.

findings.finding: Acceptance 2's 'stated bound' has no value, no measurement point, and no stated relation to one hook run's worst-case cost (each JetStream call is MaxWait 10 s, and the caches are rewatched in sequence).
findings.answer: D1 and D2: bus.RepairGrace = time.Minute, exported, equal to kvwatch's existing unrepairedDelay, which now reads it, so one constant exists. Measured from the connection event, set at both connEvents++ sites (recovery.go:50 and nats.go:921), because a cache that is not following its bucket is the fault whether the attempt is slow or failing. The hook run keeps no deadline of its own; the per-call MaxWait sum bounds it, and the plan says so.

findings.finding: Acceptance 3's baseline was measured at d4cbcfe6, not at this branch's base 88840d35, 200 clean runs only put the failure rate below about 1.5 % at 95 % confidence, and 'isolated' is undefined.
findings.answer: Section 5 names the exact loop, its working directory, serial execution, one process per run, no -race, and the measured 10.2 s per run; it adds a 49-run baseline at 88840d35 whose count is quoted whatever it is; and section 7 records that the deterministic tests prove the mechanism while the 200 runs corroborate.

findings.finding: Acceptance 4's sibling list is incomplete: #2377 (this tree's own root, which rewrites kvwatch.go and the flaky test body), #2404, #2461 and #2391 also touch these files, and 'keeps the others' tests green' has no check in this tree.
findings.answer: Section 6 names the real overlap set with the command that reads it (--paginate, never gh pr view --json files, which truncated #2446 to nothing), and turns the criterion into this tree's own steps: keep the change in four files, reintegrate per the conflicts reference when the base moves, re-run ./internal/bus/... and ./cmd/listener/..., re-run the 200 runs against the merged test body when #2377 or #2446 lands first, and send one Envoy message to the three overlapping trees.

findings.finding: Acceptance 2's parenthetical miscites INFRA-182: its failed-reconnect work was throttled WARN logging, not a health signal; its health change was the unbound durable consumer.
findings.answer: Decision 1 cites the right precedent, the terminal-watcher 503 at cmd/listener/main.go:412-416, and says that the reconnect half of the parenthetical does not support a health signal. The spec is not edited.

findings.finding: bus.Client knows no cache name, but the health answer must name a dependency.
findings.answer: D1 has HookStall return the last hook error beside the duration, and D5 writes it through writeDependencyHealth as 'KV watch rebuild', whose body carries the joined hook error (for example 'rewatch interest cache: watch role claims KV bucket: context deadline exceeded'). The signal is per bus.Client and cache-agnostic, so the nil CI cache needs no branch.

findings.finding: Leaving the deterministic test's package open decides whether /healthz is covered at all: a built-binary test cannot inject a failing Rewatch, an in-process cmd/listener test can.
findings.answer: Section 4 fixes three sites and says which clause each carries: two internal/bus tests (the retry and no ERROR, then the ERROR past the grace with HookStall), one in-process cmd/listener test for the 503 through listenerDeps and the kvCache interface, and one internal/kvwatch/repair_test.go update.

findings.finding: Two documents beyond AGENTS.md pin the /healthz answers and the hook policy: packages/envoy/docs/architecture.md and the site's health table; AGENTS.md's reconnect bullet states that recovery resubscribe failed stays an ERROR.
findings.answer: Task 6 names all of them: AGENTS.md's health bullet and its reconnect bullet, packages/envoy/docs/architecture.md (its summary row and the /healthz table), docs/site's Health and readiness section, and the changelog fragment.

findings.finding: The proposed negative control (restart NATS without JetStream) would fail the self-health pings, so runSelfHealthMonitor terminates the listener at 3 x 30 s and /healthz would already be 503 from the ping path, proving the pre-existing signal rather than the new one.
findings.answer: Section 5 replaces it: restart the server with a configuration that denies the listener's user $JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.KV_*.> only, so STREAM.INFO still answers, the pings and the durable keep passing, and only the KV watch creation fails. The plan states the monitor's threshold so the smoke's operator reads a termination as a wrong control, not a regression.

findings.finding: 'Until the listener stops' has no meaning in internal/bus, which knows only its own client, and the live-topics client reads differently.
findings.answer: D5 and the plan's scope line: the retry and the bound are per bus.Client, the stop case stays INFO (recovery.go:82-85, pinned by internal/bus/restart_test.go:384-399), and d.live carries no reconnect hook (AddReconnectHook is called only at cmd/listener/main.go:791 and bus/nats.go:341), so it is out of the health answer.

specDepartures.spec: Evidence: 'The reconnect hook gives up on one deadline-bound watch attempt, so a listener can keep serving a cache that no longer follows the bucket until the next reconnect.'
specDepartures.plan: The plan builds no retry, because main already retries: it fixes the severity of a failure the process repairs on its own (internal/bus and internal/kvwatch), states one bound of a minute, and puts a stall past that bound on /healthz. The window on main is one retry long, not 'until the next reconnect'.
specDepartures.evidence: internal/bus/recovery.go:88-93 starts go c.recover() for the same connection event; recovery.go:250-317 recoverUntilHealthy calls c.rewatch() on every attempt with no sleep before the first and a backoff of 1 s doubling to 30 s until subscriptionsHealthy() && !hooksDue() or the client stops; rewatch (recovery.go:194-210) advances hookedEvents only on success. recovery_test.go:373 TestAFailedRunOfTheReconnectHooksRunsAgainWithoutAnotherConnectionEvent pins it, and the planner ran it at base 88840d35: --- PASS (0.05s).
